text: The bytes 11000011 10101001 are UTF-8 for 'é'. Read under a single-byte encoding they display as 'Ã©'. What was lost?
choices: The second byte was reinterpreted as a control code
One byte was discarded during conversion
The original character was overwritten in memory
Nothing — only the interpretation was wrong, so the damage is often reversible
explanation: Both bytes survive intact: two bytes went in and two characters came out, exactly as the single-byte convention specifies. Only the reading was wrong, which is why this garbling can frequently be undone once you know which two encodings were involved. The distractors all imagine a destructive step that never occurred.
